pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:431 A run's expiry is only checked when an intent passes the gate. No sweep in the actor's 1 s tick (scheduler.rs tick, actor.rs loop) ever removes an expired or silent run from `runs`, and RunState has no `lost` member, so a run whose finished signal never arrives keeps its MAX_RUNS slot and shows as running.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:368 One registry (`runs` keyed by a minted ULID RunId, engines.rs:271). The Init event is a transition the registry checks and rejects when the run is not in Starting. RunState is single-sourced in table-client and generated into the client bindings.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:431 Tier one is present (EngineEvent::Init, EngineFinished). Tier two is missing: there is no staleness sweeper, no last-heard-from field and no lost state. Expiry is consulted only at the gate.

crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:300 Live runs and run history are only in memory. run.start and run.finish go to the audit chain, but startup begins with empty `runs` and `run_history` and does not reconcile a run.start that has no run.finish (left by a crash), so such a run is never declared lost.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:206 Hard concurrency cap of 4. Write scopes are disjoint: one run per deal (engines.rs:203 refuses a second run on the same deal). Each refusal reason is reported as itself.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:253 ANCHOR NOTE: the reaper itself is ActiveRun's Drop (engines.rs:31-42), which revokes the MCP grant, cancels the adapter's child and aborts the task. Removing the registry entry is what reclaims the substrate. The cited line belongs to brief-carries-the-session.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:253 Each run's brief is put together in full from the ledger projection plus the role's compiled-in playbook (and a typed brief for the policy engine), so it does not rely on the worker remembering earlier context.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:468 Each run ends in a named terminal state (Clean, Failed with a typed cause, or Cancelled) that is written to history and the audit chain, so no run silently drops off the list. There is no multi-member fan-out roster.
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:496 Whether a table can be restarted is decided from the ledger projection's `allowed` set, not from what the previous run's record says.
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:17 Runs are capped at 120 s. A pause ends runs, and resuming starts a fresh run with a new RunId, so no parked session exists to wear an old identity.
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:213 Each run uses the one selected engine. No panel of models is convened on a single question.
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:117 The executors are local CLI children on the same machine. There is no remote executor plane.
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:195 Runs are started one per deal by the owner or policy. No dispatcher model chooses how wide to fan out.

pairs.registryProposal: For short, hard-capped runs (120 s, enforced by the engine's own timeout), the rule that the tier-two sweeper is mandatory could say whether a per-run hard deadline inside the run's own task counts as the sweeper or not. Here it is the only upper bound on how long a dead run can pose as live.

A case-insensitive search of crates/table-ledger/src found no fleet, orchestrat, hibernat, heartbeat or RunState, and the run registry lives in table-runtime. The only spawn hits are std::thread::spawn in groups_tests.rs concurrency tests.
